headline: GREATLAND BEATS FY26 GUIDANCE BY 6% — 328,987 oz Gold at A$2,179 AISC; Cash Soars to A$1.29B Debt-Free (ASX/AIM/OTC: GGP)
snippet: Greatland Resources produced 328,987 ounces of gold in FY26 at an AISC of A$2,179 per ounce, exceeding the top of its guidance range (260,000–310,000 oz at A$2,400–A$2,800/oz) by 6% on volume and well below cost guidance — the Telfer-Havieron operation's strongest annual performance since its 2025 transition. The June 2026 quarter alone added 79,099 ounces and generated A$302 million in operating cash flow, lifting the company's balance sheet to approximately A$1.29 billion in cash with zero debt. The guidance beat signals operational maturity at a mid-tier that many retail investors first tracked as a junior explorer.

headline: RIO TINTO DECLARES 43% DIVIDEND SURGE — H1 EBITDA +28% to $14.8B; Copper and Lithium Now 60% of Earnings (NYSE/ASX: RIO)
snippet: Rio Tinto's first-half 2026 results were the strongest since 2022: underlying EBITDA rose 28% to $14.8 billion on $870 million in productivity savings, free cash flow surged 75%, and net profit climbed 47% to $6.66 billion. The company declared an interim dividend of $2.11 per share — up 43% year-over-year and above analyst consensus of $2.03 — and flagged a $1.8 billion annualised productivity run rate by December. For junior mining investors, the most significant signal: copper, aluminium, and lithium now account for nearly 60% of first-half EBITDA, confirming the re-rating of growth metals is flowing through to major producers' earnings.

headline: WEST AFRICAN RESOURCES POSTS RECORD Q2 — 125,179 oz Gold, A$249M Operating Cash; Sanbrado +37% on Higher Underground Grades (ASX: WAF)
source_name: Motley Fool Australia / West African Resources
snippet: West African Resources delivered its best-ever quarterly gold output in Q2 2026, mining 125,179 ounces across Sanbrado and Kiaka and generating A$249 million in operating cash flow. Sanbrado's 37% quarter-over-quarter production jump was driven by higher underground grades, while Kiaka added volume through improved mill throughput despite limited explosives supply. First-half gold production totalled 232,905 ounces, keeping West African on track for its FY26 target of 430,000 to 490,000 ounces — which, if achieved, would be a company production record.

headline: NEWCORE GOLD ENCHI GHANA: 3.67 g/t Au OVER 25.3m — Best Grade-Thickness at Nyam Yet; All 5 New Holes Hit Gold at 308m Depth (TSXV: NCAU)
snippet: Newcore Gold released July 29 the latest batch of drill results from its 80,000-metre campaign at the Enchi Gold Project in Ghana, with hole NBDD088 intersecting 3.67 g/t gold over 25.3 metres from 307.7 metres depth — the highest grade-thickness combination recorded at the Nyam Gold Deposit to date. All five new holes hit gold mineralisation, extending depth continuity within a project already holding a 51.3-million-tonne probable reserve of 1,055,000 ounces and an indicated resource of 1.5 million ounces. With multiple assay batches still pending and a resource update on the horizon, Enchi's Nyam deposit continues to prove out at depth.

headline: ALLIED GOLD Q2 ON-PLAN: 97,429 oz Produced, H1 193,445 oz — Full-Year Guidance Intact Through FOMC Volatility (NYSE: AAUF)
snippet: Allied Gold Corporation reported preliminary Q2 2026 production of 97,429 ounces of gold on July 29, bringing first-half output to 193,445 ounces — in line with operating plans and full-year guidance. The result adds to the pattern emerging across gold producers reporting this week: disciplined operators are delivering on-plan results regardless of the $4,000 price floor drama, reinforcing that the current disconnect between record earnings and depressed multiples is a sentiment problem, not a fundamentals problem.

headline: AVINO SILVER Q2: 267,305 oz Ag + 2,178 oz Au + 730K lb Cu — Mixed-Metal Profile Cushions Primary Silver Pricing Risk (TSXV: ASM)
snippet: Avino Silver & Gold Mines Ltd. (TSXV: ASM) reported Q2 2026 production of 267,305 silver ounces, 2,178 gold ounces, and 729,929 pounds of copper from its flagship Avino Mine in Mexico, for a combined 534,945 silver-equivalent ounces. The three-commodity output from a single producing mine differentiates Avino from pure-play silver juniors: copper and gold byproduct credits effectively lower the cash cost of silver production, offering partial insulation from the current spot silver weakness near multi-month lows ahead of Thursday's PCE data.

headline: NORTH AMERICAN NIOBIUM DRILLS 8-FOR-8 AT BARDY — All Quebec Pegmatite Holes Hit Target; NATO Critical Mineral Assays Pending (CSE: NIOB)
snippet: North American Niobium Corp. (CSE: NIOB) confirmed July 28 that all eight diamond drill holes in its 2026 program at the Bardy Property in Quebec's Grenville Province intersected the targeted pegmatite dyke swarm — a 100% hit rate across 1,554 metres. Targets were vectored using soil-gas radon surveys and drone-borne magnetics, with the CEO noting visual observations confirm the approach is working. Niobium is a NATO-designated critical mineral and high-strength steel additive with global supply dominated by a single Brazilian mine; Bardy's Grenville geology is analogous to the world-class Niobec mine 250 km northwest.

headline: LUNDIN HOLDS COPPER GUIDANCE AFTER CASERONES STORM HALT — Power Restoration in 2-3 Weeks; 130-140kt Cu Target Intact (TSX/NYSE: LUN)
snippet: Lundin Mining maintained its full-year 2026 copper production guidance of 130,000–140,000 tonnes at Caserones despite the mine being formally suspended on July 18 after an Atacama winter storm damaged two power-line towers and blocked access routes. A July 27 update confirmed repair crews are mobilised with full power restoration and a gradual restart expected within two to three weeks. Candelaria, Lundin's other Chilean copper complex, weathered the storm and has returned to full capacity; the company notes that Andean winter weather risk is pre-modelled into annual planning, making guidance revisions unlikely absent a significantly prolonged outage.

headline: BULGOLD COMPLETES LUTILA EPITHERMAL DRILL IN SLOVAKIA — 780m, 4 Holes Dispatched to SGS; Results Expected Late August (TSXV: ZLTO)
snippet: BULGOLD Inc. (TSXV: ZLTO) announced July 29 the completion of its maiden four-hole, 780-metre diamond drill program on the Lutila Gold Project in Central Slovakia, a 32.2 km² exploration licence prospective for quartz-adularia low-sulfidation epithermal gold mineralisation. All core samples and surface rock chip samples have been dispatched to SGS Burgas in Bulgaria, with assay results expected in late August 2026. Slovakia is an emerging EU gold exploration jurisdiction offering regulatory alignment with EU Critical Raw Materials Act frameworks and proximity to Central European processing infrastructure.

headline: GOLD SWOT: DPM METALS AND DISCOVERY SILVER +10%+ IN ONE WEEK — China's Gold Imports 76% YTD; Silver ETFs Adding Ounces on Every Dip
snippet: The weekly Gold SWOT column from US Global Investors (July 27) identifies DPM Metals and Discovery Silver as the week's standout performers — both up more than 10% — amid broadly weak gold equity sentiment. The bullish case rests on two data points: China's gold imports hit a 26-month high in May and are up 76% year-to-date, and silver ETFs added 1.09 million troy ounces in a single recent session, suggesting institutional buyers are treating every dip as an accumulation opportunity. The bear case is unchanged: hawkish Fed posture, rising real rates, and a gold mining sector that has shed $228 billion in market cap since Q1.

headline: GLD vs SLVP: SILVER MINERS OFFER 5x LEVERAGE ON A RATE CUT — But Sixth Deficit Year (46.3M oz) Still Needs the Fed to Cooperate
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis published July 28 pits GLD (physical gold ETF) against SLVP (silver miners ETF) and concludes that silver mining equities offer approximately 5x leverage to a gold price recovery — but only if the Federal Reserve begins cutting. The article anchors its structural bull case on the Silver Institute's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit projection of 46.3 million ounces for 2026, which creates upward pressure on silver prices independent of monetary policy, while cautioning that operational risk and balance sheet leverage in the mining sector amplify both upside and downside relative to physical metal.
